findings.title: Retention and TTL are not enforced by any shipped composition; evidence protection has no producer
findings.evidence: The sweep exists only as a handler: `register_retention_sweep` (retention.py:219) is reached only through `compose_worker_artifact_services` (agent_runtime_context.py:478), which `build_nexus_task_execution_registry` calls only when its optional `artifact_store` argument is given. The only shipped caller, `applications/_shared/queue_worker_wiring.py:86` (`create_nexus_celery_worker_app`), passes none. `ARTIFACT_RETENTION_SWEEP_TASK_NAME` is referenced only inside retention.py: nothing in product code builds or submits a sweep task (compare `memory_retention_sweep_task_request` for the memory plane). `ArtifactRetentionPolicy.retain_hours` has one consumer, the optional `policy` argument of `resolve_expiry`, which no product caller supplies; `delete_on_task_complete` and `archive_to_object_store` have none (grep over intergrax/ agents/ applications/). `ArtifactRetentionClass.AUDIT_EVIDENCE` is assigned by no product code (only enum, `resolve_expiry` and `protection_reason` mention it), so the 'audit evidence is never deletable' invariant protects nothing that the platform produces. The B-D8 unit tests exercise the sweep with a harness-built store, registry and clock.
findings.reproduction: git grep -n 'ARTIFACT_RETENTION_SWEEP_TASK_NAME\|AUDIT_EVIDENCE\|retain_hours\|delete_on_task_complete' -- intergrax agents applications ':!*tests*'; git grep -n 'artifact_store' -- applications intergrax/applications (no assignment of RuntimeContext.artifact_store or worker artifact_store).
findings.impact: TTL expiry (FRZ-SEC-09) and the evidence/legal-hold deletion guarantees hold for the library and for hosts that wire it by hand; a default host never deletes an expired artifact, never admits the sweep, and never classifies anything as audit evidence.
findings.repair: Orchestrator decision whether host composition is a PDC-X claim (as for dossier F-04). If yes: (a) composition root passes the persistence bundle's `artifact_store`, a governance port and a durable audit recorder into the worker bootstrap and into `RuntimeContext`; (b) add a sweep task-request builder and an admission/schedule trigger next to the sweep; (c) give `ArtifactRetentionPolicy` a real consumer or retire the dead fields; (d) give evidence artifacts a producer that sets AUDIT_EVIDENCE.
findings.verification: CODE_READ + GREP (reproducible); unit mechanism re-run green (134 passed)

findings.title: The D8 runtime (durable store, governed port, spill, reference chain) is dormant in shipped hosts, and the spill round trip has no resolver in product code
findings.evidence: No product code assigns `RuntimeContext.artifact_store` (field default None, agent_runtime_context.py:126), so `_spill_large_tool_output` (plan_context_invocation.py:65) is inert. `GovernedArtifactReadPort` is constructed only in `compose_worker_artifact_services`; `ArtifactReferenceResolver`, `reference_fragment`, `REFERENCE_TOOL_NAME` (no tool of that name is registered) and `CollaborativeWorkContentSource` have no non-test caller; no read source is registered for the `context` or `business` class in any composition. If a host does set a store, a tool output over 16 KiB is replaced in the model-visible message by a 512-char preview plus `artifact://...` marker (plan_context_invocation.py:77) that nothing in the runtime can turn back into content. The spill also records only run_id (no task_id, trace_id, workspace_id; `agent_id` may be empty string), so the lineage promised for R004 is thin on the one product path that writes artifacts. `RunArtifactBundle.durable_refs` and `ArtifactRef.to_durable_ref` have no product caller.
findings.impact: Rows R006/R007/R010/R012/R013 close at library level only; enabling spill alone would lose tool output for the agent.
findings.repair: Same composition decision as F-D8-01; additionally a registered `artifact.reference` read tool (through the governed port) and a reference-fragment injection point must ship together with spill, or spill must stay off.

findings.title: Raw object-storage tools (`storage.get/put/delete/exists`) bypass the governed artifact port and the tenant check
findings.evidence: ADR-PDC-08 closed `storage.presigned_url` (fails closed) but its siblings in tools/providers/storage/service.py take any key and act on the same `ObjectStorage` that backs Collaborative Work content (key = `intergrax/collaborative-work/artifact-content/v1/<sha256(tenant NUL workspace)>/sha256/<digest>`, derivable from public ids plus a content digest). They carry no tenant or prefix binding, no artifact authorization and no GovernanceAuditEvent; `get`/`exists` are risk LOW, `put`/`delete` HIGH. Probe P4 (ia_d8_probes_1.py): content stored for tenant 'tenant-victim' is returned by `storage_get`, reported by `storage_exists` and removed by `storage_delete` with no check.
findings.reproduction: PYTHONPATH=. uv run python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D8/adversarial_scripts/ia_d8_probes_1.py  (probe P4_storage_tools_bypass; log logs/probes_1.log)
findings.impact: An agent holding the storage capability can read, overwrite or hard-delete business artifact content outside the governed port; delete also defeats the 'Collaborative Work has no hard-delete API' claim (R009). Exploitation needs the content digest, so the cross-tenant read risk is bounded; the missing governance is not.
findings.repair: Bind storage tool keys to the caller tenant (prefix) and refuse the Collaborative Work content prefix, or route the tools through the governed port; add a gate like the presign gate that fails if an ungoverned tool can address the content prefix.

findings.title: Governed read: workspace scope is optional and the capability is tenant-wide
findings.evidence: governed_access.py:283 checks the stored workspace only `if request.workspace_id is not None`; authorization is the tenant-level capability `artifact.read`, with no run or principal binding. Probe P6: an artifact stored in 'ws-1' is read with no workspace_id, denied only for a wrong one. Same for download, legal hold and delete requests. Re-verified from dossier lead F-01.
findings.impact: Any holder of `artifact.read` in a tenant reads any execution-evidence or tool-output artifact of that tenant by id (markers carry the id).
findings.repair: Derive the workspace (or a run/principal binding) from `ArtifactAccessContext` or make it mandatory in `ArtifactReadRequest` for classes that store it; add a negative test.

findings.title: Retention sweep can delete without any audit record and deletes versions written after the expiry selection
findings.evidence: `ArtifactRetentionSweeper(audit=None)` deletes and records nothing (`_record` returns when no auditor; worker_bootstrap passes `artifact_audit=None` by default). `sweep()` selects expired latest versions, then `delete_artifact` removes EVERY version: probe F02 (in-memory and SQLite) puts a non-expiring v2 after selection and the delete leaves 0 versions. Re-verified from dossier lead F-02.
findings.reproduction: PYTHONPATH=. uv run python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D8/adversarial_scripts/ia_d8_probes_2.py  (probes F02_toctou..., F02_sweep_without_audit...)
findings.impact: Destructive background deletion with optional evidence; a newer retained version can be destroyed by a sweep that selected an older expired one.
findings.repair: Refuse to construct the sweeper without an audit recorder on product profiles; delete conditionally on the version/expiry observed (compare-and-delete inside the store transaction).

findings.title: Expired artifacts stay readable and downloadable until a sweep runs
findings.evidence: `GovernedArtifactReadPort.read`/`issue_download_url` and `ExecutionArtifactSource` never consult `expires_at_utc`. Probe P5: an artifact whose TTL ended 30 days earlier is read successfully.
findings.impact: With F-D8-01 (no scheduled sweep) the TTL is neither enforced at rest nor at read; ephemeral tool output outlives its retention class.
findings.repair: Treat an expired, unprotected artifact as not found in the source or the port (clock already injected) and test it.

findings.title: The runtime gateway for execution artifacts (`RuntimeContext.create_artifact`) cannot work: it omits the required tenant_id
findings.evidence: agent_runtime_context.py:235 builds `Artifact(...)` without `tenant_id` (a required field since commit 4f7517050); calling it raises `TypeError: Artifact.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'tenant_id'` (probe logs/probe_create_artifact.log). It has no caller anywhere in intergrax/, agents/, applications/ or tests/. It also sets no producer, lineage, retention class or expiry. Pre-existing (e8064d72e), not introduced by B-D8, but it is the documented gateway of the D8 execution-evidence class; the only product code that writes `Artifact` objects is the spill path.
findings.impact: No execution-evidence artifact of class `execution_evidence` can be produced by the runtime; R004 producer/lineage and R007 durability have no real writer.
findings.repair: Fix the gateway (tenant from `state`, producer and lineage from the run identity, retention class) and add a test that calls it against a SQLite store; or remove it and name the real writer.

findings.title: GovernedArtifactReadPort._guard ignores the authorization decision value
findings.evidence: `authorize_tool` result is discarded (governed_access.py `_guard`); fail-closed only because the real boundary raises. Probe F10: a governance port returning a DENY decision without raising lets the read succeed. Re-verified from dossier lead F-10.
findings.impact: Any other `AgentRuntimeGovernancePort` implementation that returns instead of raising grants access.
findings.repair: Check the returned decision in `_guard` and deny on anything but ALLOW.

findings.title: Sweep robustness: starvation by protected rows, one poisoned row aborts the sweep, naive/aware datetimes, negative limit
findings.evidence: P7: with limit=5 and five expired legal-hold artifacts that sort first, `sweep` examines only those, deletes nothing and a second sweep repeats it, so an unprotected expired artifact is never reached. P8: a tampered SQLite row makes `list_expired` raise `ArtifactDigestMismatchError`; the sweep aborts for the whole tenant. F28: a naive `expires_at_utc` makes the in-memory `list_expired` raise TypeError; a negative `limit` slices off the last candidate in memory and means unlimited in SQLite. Re-verified from dossier lead F-28.
findings.reproduction: PYTHONPATH=. uv run python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D8/adversarial_scripts/ia_d8_probes_1.py (P7, P8) and ia_d8_probes_2.py (F28_*)
findings.impact: Availability and accuracy of retention under hold-heavy or corrupted data; no data disclosure.
findings.repair: Skip protected rows in the candidate query (or page past them), catch and report per-artifact load failures, normalize datetimes at `Artifact` construction, validate `limit` >= 1.

findings.title: A v1 `ArtifactRef` retention class that is not an exact enum value silently becomes `default`
findings.evidence: `_retention_class_from_str` (artifact_ref.py:222) falls back to DEFAULT. Probe P3: 'audit_evidence' stays, but 'AUDIT_EVIDENCE', 'audit-evidence' and 'evidence' become 'default' in the durable reference (fail-open for the one class that must never be deletable).
findings.impact: A mislabelled evidence artifact loses its deletion protection without any error.
findings.repair: Raise a typed error for an unknown retention class during migration.

findings.title: Digest validators accept a trailing newline
findings.evidence: `_DIGEST_RE = ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` with `re.match` accepts `sha256:<hex>\n` (probe P2: True). Same pattern in task_artifacts `_SHA256_HEX_RE`. A reference carrying such a value validates but can never verify its content.
findings.impact: Malformed digests enter durable references; mismatch is only detected at verification time.
findings.repair: Use `fullmatch` or `\Z` in both validators; add a negative test.

findings.title: Backend failures during an artifact operation leave no outcome event
findings.evidence: `_guard` audits a fixed exception list (not found, denied, deletion refused, digest mismatch, download unavailable). Probe P10: a source raising RuntimeError produces only the authorization event; no `artifact.read.outcome` event. Same for sqlite or validation errors. Re-verified from dossier lead F-28.
findings.impact: An authorized operation that fails unexpectedly is not in the evidence trail (R016: one event per operation outcome).
findings.repair: Add a catch-all that records a DENY/ERROR outcome event and re-raises.

findings.title: `reconstruct_artifact_lineage` does not check tenant or workspace of ancestors
findings.evidence: Probe P9: a child of tenant-A whose parent reference belongs to tenant-OTHER reconstructs as ['tenant-OTHER/p', 'tenant-A/c']. Parents are matched by id and digest only.
findings.impact: A pool mixing tenants can chain across tenants; callers must pre-filter. No store or port feeds this function today.
findings.repair: Require identical `scope.tenant_id` along the chain and raise `ArtifactLineageError` otherwise.

findings.title: Legal hold: SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE` overwrites the holder and reason; the in-memory store drops them; release needs no ownership
findings.evidence: Probes P13/P14: a second `place_legal_hold` replaces ('legal-counsel','litigation') by ('other-agent','x'); `InMemoryArtifactStore._holds` keeps only (tenant, artifact). `release_legal_hold` removes any hold for any caller with `artifact.legal_hold`.
findings.reproduction: PYTHONPATH=. uv run python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D8/adversarial_scripts/ia_d8_probes_1.py  (probes P13, P14)
findings.impact: The legal-hold trail is lossy and overwritable by a second holder.
findings.repair: Keep holds append-only (hold id per holder) and release only the caller's hold, or record holder changes as events.

findings.title: Run artifact bundle builder follows file symlinks under the sandbox root, and bundle entry types still allow an empty sha256
findings.evidence: `_sandbox_artifact_refs` uses `rglob('*')`, `is_file()` and `read_bytes()` (all follow symlinks) and publishes the sha256 of the target. NOT reproduced: this host cannot create symlinks (WinError 1314); finding stands on code reading. `ApplicationArtifactRef/WorkspaceArtifactRef/SandboxArtifactRef.sha256` default to '' and are validated only for format; the digest becomes mandatory only in `RunArtifactBundle.durable_refs`, which has no product caller (F-D8-02). From dossier lead F-27.
findings.reproduction: Code reading of intergrax/runtime/nexus/orchestration/run_artifact_bundle_builder.py (_sandbox_artifact_refs); probe F27 in ia_d8_probes_2.py logs the symlink limitation.
findings.impact: Hash oracle for a file outside the sandbox (read pre-dates the batch); bundle metadata can carry no digest.
findings.repair: Skip symlinks and verify `resolve()` stays under the root; make `sha256` required on new bundle entries or project through `durable_refs` at publication.

findings.title: Test strength: no hostile-source or shipped-composition test; two tenant checks unpinned
findings.evidence: No D8/XD test uses a source that returns another tenant's reference (grep `tenant_mismatch` in tests/qualification/pdc_x: all assertions are request-tenant mismatches); the stored-tenant re-check in `read` is therefore unpinned (probe_hostile_source shows it works today). No test composes a default host and asserts that a sweep is registered or the port exists; the P6-R wiring tests assert helper behaviour. Re-verified from dossier lead F-29.
findings.reproduction: grep -rn 'tenant_mismatch' tests/qualification/pdc_x ; PYTHONPATH=. uv run python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D8/adversarial_scripts/ia_d8_probe_hostile_source.py
findings.impact: Defence-in-depth checks and the wiring claims can regress unnoticed.
findings.repair: Add a hostile-source test and a composition test that fails when the shipped worker bootstrap registers no artifact sweep.

findings.title: Documentation and ownership inconsistencies, residual alias use
findings.evidence: (a) PDC_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX row says `application_artifacts.py` 'is removed'; ADR says remove 'under COMPAT-X R5 shim policy'; the code keeps a re-export shim (consistent with the architecture doc, not with the matrix). (b) plan/ARTIFACT_LIFECYCLE.md 'Open items' still lists hub registration and an artifact store opener as open; both exist (capabilities/README.md:79, sqlite_opens.py:87). (c) The R015 matrix row cites `CURRENT_HEAD_DELTA` '0 files (llm_adapters)', unrelated to content_storage; the real delta since EBH-5 (33ecf19cc) is one file, cosmetic plus the read-only helper `artifact_content_object_key`. (d) taxonomy.py names `tool_runtime.py` as owner of `tool_output` while the spill lives in nexus/artifacts/spill.py. (e) `runtime/observability/emitter.py:39` still imports `ArtifactRef` from the bridge under TYPE_CHECKING (resolves only through the module `__getattr__` shim; invisible to type checkers).
findings.impact: Reviewers can read the wrong closure state.
findings.repair: Reconcile the ownership matrix and plan doc at P8; switch the emitter annotation to `TraceArtifactRef`.

findings.title: The B-D8 implementation commit carries an AI-attribution trailer
findings.evidence: `git show 92ee26bf3` ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; the repo rule `intergrax-no-ai-attribution` forbids it. The commit is merged history.
findings.impact: Process only; no product effect.
findings.repair: None required for history; noted for CERT.

findings.title: Adjacent partial-results test is red (not D8 evidence)
findings.evidence: tests/unit/runtime/long_running/test_partial_results.py::test_build_task_progress_view_aggregates_checkpoints fails (`human_request_expires_at` is None; the fixture hard-codes 2026-05-27, before the audit date, cause not investigated). The R011 claim (artifacts do not own partial results) is structural and verified separately.
findings.impact: None on D8.
findings.repair: Owner of long_running tests.

findings.title: Known classified reds and the R-05 exit hang were not reproduced in D8 runs
findings.evidence: The three D8-scope pytest commands exited on their own (exit 0). `xd_03` (the dossier F-09 trigger) was not run. EBH-7 identity, roadmap_replay_x and dist_scale_x/Docker were not run and are not re-reported.
findings.impact: None.
findings.repair: None.
